reason:
Compared the entire original lem:rot at source lines 395-426, all five numbered clauses, the preceding regular/principal-turn definitions, and the source's labelled/cyclic-equivariant conventions with SM.rotation_number and every concrete definition and supporting proof supplying its meaning. The aggregate retains the printed n>=3 and actual Regular P domain for the same real planar labelled tuple P. Its NeZero n instance is redundant under n>=3 and introduces no additional mathematical size restriction. It does not require Generic, globally distinct vertices, no self-crossings, all turns nonzero, a chosen lift of edge angles, or any desired rotation law as a premise. The regular domain continues to admit positive collinear consecutive edges. The leading equality uses exactly the source normalization: the actual finite sum of principal turns multiplied by 1/(2*pi).

Clause (i) is actual integer-valued rotation, stated as the existence of an integer whose real cast equals that normalized sum. The principal turn is the already reviewed argument of conjugate(incoming complex edge) times outgoing complex edge, with the actual Euclidean normalization and source determinant orientation. In the inspected pinned Mathlib Real.Angle type, which is the additive circle of period 2*pi, argument multiplication and conjugation make this principal turn equal the difference of the actual outgoing and incoming edge arguments. Summing telescopes through the bijection i->i-1 of the finite cyclic index set. The proved zero-angle-class characterization gives an integer multiple of 2*pi, and division by that positive period gives the integer witness. This does not replace the actual sum with rounding or assume an integer-valued definition.

Clause (ii) quantifies over every endpoint Q, every actual continuous Path P Q whose values are regular throughout the closed unit interval, and every pair of interval parameters s and t. Thus it proves constancy along the whole path, not merely endpoint equality or a chosen path. The underlying theorem is stronger in an appropriate direction: every continuous regular family on an arbitrary preconnected parameter space has equal values at every two parameters. Its proof first establishes actual principal-angle continuity by composing the continuous coordinate-complex rotor with the real-valued argument on the exact regular slit-plane domain. Positive collinearity is allowed there, and no global branch choice for individual edge directions or uniform angular bound is required. Finite summation gives continuity, and the independently proved integer range is discrete in the reals, yielding constancy by preconnectedness. Cyclic invariance of the actual sum is separately proved by reindexing i->i+a. This supplies the source's explicit permission to work throughout on labelled tuples with recorded equivariance; no unproved path-lifting premise or combinatorial replacement of the regular locus is used.

Both parts of clause (iii) are now implemented. For insertion, insertVertex P i t is an actual LabelledTuple (n+1), constructed by first choosing the cyclic cut at the old vertex i+1 and appending one new vertex on the resulting wrap edge. Its old entries equal P(j+(i+1)) and its new entry is exactly edgePoint P i t. The shift j->j+(i+1) enumerates every original index in cyclic traversal order, without requiring the vertex coordinates themselves to be distinct. insertIndex embeds each old natural residue into ZMod(n+1); its injectivity, disjointness from the new residue n, and exhaustive coverage together with that one new residue are proved. insertIndex_next preserves successive old indices away from the cut, insertIndex_last_add_one joins the old last vertex to the inserted one, and insertedIndex_add_one joins the inserted one to the old first vertex. The predecessor formulas cover both corresponding incoming-edge cases. Consequently this is an actual single-vertex subdivision of the chosen directed edge, not an arbitrary tuple with a supplied desirable turn inventory. The use of a cut at i+1 is compatible with the source's representative convention and the chosen edge is explicit data.

The insertion claim quantifies over every original i and every real t with 0<t<1. Its new-point equality and proved edgeInterior membership cover the source's arbitrary relative-interior point because the inherited edgeInterior is exactly that strict affine parameterization. For the wrap-edge construction, every unaffected outgoing edge is unchanged, the old last outgoing edge becomes t times the old edge, and the new outgoing edge is (1-t) times that old edge. The old first incoming edge is the corresponding (1-t) multiple; all other old incoming edges are unchanged. These formulas are derived from the newly constructed vertex coordinates. The independent positive-rescaling theorem proves invariance of the actual argument under scaling the incoming and outgoing vectors by possibly different positive numbers, since their rotor is multiplied by their positive product. It also proves preservation of the complete RegularPair domain. Applying it to the actual edge formulas proves every old principal turn unchanged and every old corner still regular, including formerly zero turns from positive collinearity. At the new vertex both incident edges are positive multiples of the same nonzero old edge, so its actual principal turn is zero and it is regular. The exhaustive new-index decomposition then proves the entire inserted tuple regular. Finally, sum_insertion_indices proves the finite-sum reindexing from the full new universe to the injectively retained old universe plus the unique new index; inserting the proved turn identities yields equality of the actual principal-turn sums and normalized rotations. Shift invariance transfers this calculation to every original edge, including the wrap edge. There is no additional restriction excluding intersections of the inserted point with other edges or old vertices.

For reversal, the actual inherited reversal is P(2-i), with reversed edge -edge P(1-i). The proof transforms each original pair (u,v) to (-v,-u): the dot product and product of Euclidean lengths are unchanged, the determinant is negated, and -theta stays within the strict principal interval. It therefore satisfies the exact reversed cosine/sign specification. Previously proved uniqueness gives principalTurn(reversal P,i)=-principalTurn(P,2-i); existence gives preservation of regularity. Reindexing the actual sum by the bijection i->2-i yields exactly negated rotation. Reversal is not confused with a cyclic relabelling.

Clause (iv) is conditional on n=3 for the same P appearing in the aggregate, rather than a statement about an unrelated supplied triangle. Its supporting proof derives the nonzero common triangle determinant from regularity and actual edge closure: if the first two regular edges had zero determinant they would be positive multiples, so their closing third edge would be a forbidden negative multiple of the second. Actual coordinate calculations show every corner determinant is the same. The nonzero common sign makes all three principal turns strictly positive or all strictly negative; their normalized sum has that sign. Integrality and the independently proved strict bound then force it to be the corresponding integer 1 or -1. The aggregate states equality with every actual turn P i, membership in {1,-1}, and nonzero rotation, covering all three source labels.

Clause (v) is exactly 2*abs(rotationNumber P)<n. It follows from the strict principal-angle bound abs(theta_i)<pi at each regular corner, strict finite summation on the nonempty cyclic index set, the triangle inequality for the actual signed sum, and division by positive pi. No nonzero-rotation or nonzero-turn premise is added. The final cyclic-shift equality applies to every representative shift and the actual sum; together with the source's explicitly authorized labelled/equivariant convention it gives the full polygon reading without a distinguished vertex.

The source hash, all 24 inspected local supporting-file hashes, and the independently recomputed semantic dependency hash match the passed checkpoint-021 development receipt. The seven new insertion/aggregate modules are unchanged from this review. The seventeen inherited files match the prior independent regular/reversal reviews and partial rotation checkpoint-020 inventory. That earlier report accurately recorded insertion as missing at checkpoint 020; the actual insertion construction and proof inspected here now close that gap. The current receipt audits 746 project declarations and 18 mapped claims with only the standard propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound axioms, and explicitly leaves stage_accepted false. This review certifies the complete original PROVE row lem:rot only. It does not certify lem:uniformrot, the corner state sum, or the main wall-crossing/soft-theorem targets. The index, scaling, continuity and other supporting lemmas do not add separate original claims. No Lean or declaration-map file was authored or edited by this reviewer.

countersignature_20260913.reason: SM.rotation_number (work/lean/SM/RotationTheorem.lean:15-31) states every clause of the printed lem:rot (reference/SM/sm-1-polygons.tex:407-421; blueprint extract identical apart from the status tag; not listed in CHANGES_SINCE_20260909.md section 1, consistent with sm15_reworded=false) on the same domain. Domain: hn : 3 ≤ n, P : LabelledTuple n = ZMod n → ℝ×ℝ, Regular P := ∀ i, edge(i-1) ≠ 0 ∧ edge i ≠ 0 ∧ ¬∃ r<0, edge i = r•edge(i-1) (RegularLocus.lean:12-13, RegularPairs.lean:8-9), which is exactly the regular locus of def:regular (source 386-396) in the labelled-tuple reading the source's formalization remark (55-62) explicitly permits; the extra [NeZero n] is implied by 3 ≤ n. principalTurn P i = arg(conj(ℓ_{i-1})·ℓ_i) (RegularLocus.lean:15-16, RegularPairs.lean:54, EuclideanPlane.lean:55) with re = dot and im = det, and principalAngle_spec / principalAngle_existsUnique_iff (PrincipalAngles.lean:9-15, 63-64) identify it with the printed unique angle in (-π,π) with the cosine/sign specification, so it denotes ϑ_i; rotationNumber P = (Σ principalTurn)/(2π) (RotationNumber.lean:10-11) is the printed rot, and the first conjunct restates the normalization. (i) ∃ k:ℤ, rot P = k. (ii) ∀ Q, ∀ γ : Path P Q (Mathlib continuous path, standard Pi/product topology on (ℝ²)^n, no custom instance), values regular throughout → rot(γ s) = rot(γ t) for all s,t: every continuous path in ℛ_n, since P is arbitrary regular. (iii) insertVertex P i t = appendVertex (shift (i+1) P) t (VertexInsertion.lean:11-12, InsertedTuple.lean:11-12) is the (n+1)-tuple (μ_{i+1},…,μ_i, μ_i + tℓ_i) for every edge i and every 0<t<1, with the new point asserted ∈ edgeInterior P i (Polygon.lean:57-58), the result asserted Regular, and rot unchanged; reversal P i = P(2-i) (Reversal.lean:11) is exactly def:shift, with Regular (reversal P) ∧ rot(reversal P) = -rot P. (iv) n=3 → ∀ i, rot P = (turn P i : ℝ) (turn = χ_{i-1,i,i+1} = sign det, Chirotope.lean:10-14; standard SignType→ℝ cast) ∧ rot ∈ {1,-1} ∧ rot ≠ 0. (v) 2·|rot P| < n. The final conjunct ∀ a, rot(shift a P) = rot P is the shift-equivariance the source remark asks a labelled formalization to record, and makes the chosen insertion representative cover the polygon-level statement. No hypotheses added, no clause weakened, nothing vacuous (a regular triangle and a constant path satisfy all hypotheses). Independently agrees with the accepted review in work/reviews/lem-rot.json.
